**Fix for Windows PowerShell 5.1 (scripts started with `-File`), a CI gate in the release process, and consistent reporting instructions.**

> **Use 2.0.3 instead of 2.0.2.** In 2.0.2 the scripts could fail under Windows PowerShell 5.1 when they were started with `powershell.exe -File`, which is how the scheduled tasks start. The CI job on Windows PowerShell 5.1, new in 2.0.2, found it after the release. The 2.x scripts have not run in a domain yet; the lab validation (L1-L20) is in progress ([docs/VALIDATION.md](https://github.com/mayer-bautechnik/cloudsync-soa-toolkit/blob/v2.0.3/docs/VALIDATION.md)).

## Fixed

- `$PSScriptRoot` can be empty in parameter default values under Windows PowerShell 5.1 with `-File`, so the default `-ConfigPath` could not be built.
  - All scripts, tools and tests now resolve their folder at the start, with a fallback to `$MyInvocation.MyCommand.Definition`.
  - `-ConfigPath`, `-Path` and `-Root` get their defaults after `param()`.
- Tests and tools build child paths without mixing `/` and `\`.

## Changed

- **Release process** ([docs/RELEASING.md](https://github.com/mayer-bautechnik/cloudsync-soa-toolkit/blob/v2.0.3/docs/RELEASING.md)):
  - push the commit, then wait until both CI jobs are green, then create the signed tag and publish;
  - `tools/Build-SoaRelease.ps1` refuses to build when the CI runs of the commit are not all successful;
  - a new section describes how to handle a broken, already published (immutable) release: fix forward, never move a published tag.
- `tools/Invoke-SoaStaticChecks.ps1` also runs the tests and the claims check under Windows PowerShell 5.1 when started from PowerShell 7 on Windows.
- **Reporting:**
  - the prerequisites, monitoring, impact and test scripts point out that their reports contain environment names and are shared through `Export-SoaReport.ps1`;
  - CONTRIBUTING, README, OPERATIONS, REPORTING, AGENTS and the issue forms describe the same process;
  - new issue form *Question or idea*.

## Upgrade from 2.0.2

1. Replace the scripts with this release. Keep your `SoaToolkit.config.psd1`; there are no new keys.
2. If 2.0.2 is already deployed to hosts, update the scripts there:
   ```powershell
   .\Install-SoaToolkit.ps1 -Step DeployTasks
   ```

Details: [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/mayer-bautechnik/cloudsync-soa-toolkit/blob/v2.0.3/CHANGELOG.md)

## Verify the download

Compare the SHA-256 of the asset with the digest GitHub shows next to it. The zip contains `SHA256SUMS.txt` for every file:

```powershell
Get-FileHash .\cloudsync-soa-toolkit-2.0.3.zip -Algorithm SHA256
Get-ChildItem -Recurse | Unblock-File
```

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/mayer-bautechnik/cloudsync-soa-toolkit/compare/v2.0.2...v2.0.3
